key_points: More than 20 lawmakers are supporting tougher artificial intelligence rules following warnings from Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon that AI labs are gambling with lives.
items.summary: More than 20 lawmakers are supporting tougher artificial intelligence rules after Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon warned that AI labs are gambling with lives. Sen. Ruben Gallego urged Senate leadership to form a bipartisan AI select committee, while Rep. Lori Trahan stated cross-party momentum has reached a tipping point. Several bills, including the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, are already in motion, though prospects for passage remain remote with Congress largely on recess. President Donald Trump dismissed extinction concerns, while OpenAI's Chris Lehane called for mandatory national regulation.
items.title: Lawmakers push AI regulation after researcher extinction warning

key_points: Oracle shares gained 3 per cent after a $26 billion revenue backlog jump eased worries about its debt-driven spending, though analysts noted cash flow recovery remains distant.
The company reported negative free cash flow of $5.40 billion, which was better than the $9.56 billion analysts estimated, according to LSEG data.
items.summary: Oracle shares rose 3 per cent on Friday following a $26 billion increase in revenue backlog, which alleviated some investor concerns regarding the company's debt-fueled expansion. While Oracle stated that roughly half of its $664 billion backlog will convert to sales within 36 months, Morningstar analyst Luke Yang noted that cash flow improvements are not expected soon. The company reported negative free cash flow of $5.40 billion, surpassing analyst estimates of $9.56 billion according to LSEG data. Despite these figures, Evercore analysts described the results as a solid step forward, though the stock still trades at a lower multiple than Microsoft and Amazon.
items.title: Oracle shares rise as AI backlog growth offsets spending concerns

The Wall Street Journal reports that China's semiconductor export value went up 130% from last year, even though chip export volume went down by 7.9%.

key_points: Escalating tariffs between the U.S. and Canada threaten the deeply integrated North American auto supply chain.
Analysts warn that smaller suppliers face significant financial trouble while major companies struggle with long-term planning uncertainty.
Industry leaders describe the situation as chaotic, noting that reconfiguring supply chains would be costly and time-consuming.
items.summary: The escalating trade war between the U.S. and Canada is creating significant challenges for the tightly woven auto-parts industry. New tariffs on steel, aluminum, and vehicles threaten to disrupt decades of cross-border manufacturing integration. Dan Hearsch of AlixPartners states that the tariffs make industry planning difficult, adding to existing post-pandemic supply chain issues. Jim Jarrell of Linamar Corporation notes that altering supply chains would require substantial time and cost. While major suppliers like Bosch and Magna are monitoring the situation, smaller businesses face potential financial trouble. Economists warn that the industry cannot move as quickly as political changes, leaving companies hesitant to invest or reconfigure operations amidst uncertainty.
items.title: U.S.-Canada trade war creates supply chain headaches for auto parts makers

key_points: US inflation held steady at 3.4% in August, driven by a 3.9% rise in gasoline prices, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
Market expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike next week have reached 85% as traders anticipate further measures to combat persistent price increases.
items.summary: US inflation remained unchanged at 3. 4% in August, with gasoline prices rising 3. 9% and pushing the overall rate above the Federal Reserve's 2% target, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported. Diesel prices hit a new high above $6 per gallon, fueled by global oil price spikes linked to US-Iran conflict escalations. Consequently, 85% of traders now expect the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates by a quarter percentage point next week to slow price increases, despite Chair Kevin Warsh remaining tight-lipped on specific decisions.
items.title: US inflation remains steady at 3.4% as diesel prices exceed $6 per gallon

key_points: Lawrence Wright's book The Looming Tower describes the bureaucratic failures that allowed Al-Qaeda operatives to enter the US.
The author tells the story primarily through the lives of Osama bin Laden, Ayman al-Zawahiri, Prince Turki al-Faisal, and John O'Neill.
items.summary: Lawrence Wright's Pulitzer Prize-winning book, The Looming Tower, presents a painstaking record of bureaucratic failure leading to the September 11 attacks. The author notes that the CIA knew two Al-Qaeda operatives were in the US for over a year before informing the FBI. Wright primarily tells the narrative through the lives of four key individuals, including Osama bin Laden and FBI agent John O'Neill.
items.title: Lawrence Wright details CIA and FBI failures in 9/11 book

key_points: Democratic Senator Ron Wyden and Republican Congressman Warren Davidson wrote to the UK investigatory powers tribunal demanding transparency in Apple's legal challenge.
The bipartisan pair argued that British secrecy orders improperly restrict US congressional oversight of the dispute over iCloud encryption.
items.summary: Democratic Senator Ron Wyden and Republican Congressman Warren Davidson sent a letter to the UK investigatory powers tribunal urging it to disclose details of Apple's legal case. The bipartisan pair warned that British secrecy directives needlessly strain US-UK relations and improperly limit US congressional oversight. They argued the UK government cannot use administrative gag orders to override the constitutional authority of the US legislature while championing legislative scrutiny at home. The letter targets a case-management hearing scheduled for this month regarding Apple's challenge to the government's power to issue technical capability notices.
items.title: US lawmakers urge British court to open Apple case

key_points: Anthropic reported that a Yemeni cell used its Claude chatbot to develop software for guided rockets and missiles.
The company stated the actors tested a rocket but failed, subsequently returning to the AI for assistance.
items.summary: Anthropic revealed that a Yemeni cell utilized its Claude chatbot to create guidance software for weapons. The firm reported identifying actors developing a guided rocket, a ballistic missile, and a hypersonic variant. Anthropic stated the group tested a rocket, which failed, prompting them to return to the AI for help. The company banned the accounts involved in the illegal activity.
items.title: Anthropic reveals Yemen fighters used its AI to build guided weapons

key_points: Anthony Moretti states that the wars launched after 9/11 resulted in approximately 940,000 deaths between 2001 and 2023, with half being innocent civilians.
The author reports that American public opinion has shifted, with roughly 50% now viewing the Iraq war as a mistake compared to 25% two decades ago.
Moretti concludes that Western policy must alter its military-first approach to the Middle East to foster stability and avoid further instability.
items.summary: Anthony Moretti, a special commentator for CGTN, argues that the United States has failed to learn lessons from the September 11 attacks over the past 25 years. He states that subsequent wars in Iraq and Afghanistan caused staggering loss of life, with the Watson School of International and Public Affairs at Brown University noting approximately 940,000 deaths in the region by 2023. Moretti reports that while public opinion once supported the wars, roughly 50% of Americans now view the Iraq conflict as a mistake. He asserts that the 'war on terror' did not eliminate hostility and that America's international standing remains damaged. The commentator suggests that a pivot away from military-first strategies toward reasonable diplomacy is necessary to prevent further instability in the Middle East.
items.title: Commentator argues 9/11 lessons remain unlearned after two decades of conflict

The expanded BRICS group now represents roughly half of humanity and 40% of global GDP with ten partner countries joining the original members.
India pursued a whole-of-nation approach to host nearly 400 meetings across over 30 cities, resulting in concrete initiatives like a Digital Agriculture network.
items.summary: Vikram Doraiswami, Ambassador of India to China, describes New Delhi's preparation for the fourth BRICS summit, themed Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The article notes the group has expanded to include ten partner countries, representing roughly half of humanity and 40% of global GDP. Doraiswami explains India's chairship focused on four pillars: resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability, executed through a whole-of-nation approach hosting nearly 400 meetings across over 30 cities. The author emphasizes that stable India-China cooperation is vital for BRICS credibility, citing recent working-level engagement and shared development goals between the two largest emerging economies.
items.title: India hosts BRICS summit focusing on resilience and innovation

key_points: Twenty-five years after 9/11, al Qaeda has evolved from a centralized global network into a decentralized force of regional affiliates causing instability across Africa, the Middle East, and Asia.

Experts warn that the US administration has downgraded the threat of Islamist terrorism in favor of criminal cartels, leading to budget cuts and personnel losses within the counterterrorism architecture.

While transnational attacks on Western soil have diminished, regional branches like JNIM and al Shabaab continue to operate effectively, with some affiliates even receiving ransom funds from other groups.
items.summary: Twenty-five years after the September 11 attacks, al Qaeda persists as a destabilizing force, though its structure has shifted from a centralized global jihad to a network of regional affiliates. Bruce Hoffman of the Council on Foreign Relations noted that the organization has devolved authority to dozens of franchises, particularly active in the Sahel, Somalia, and Afghanistan. Wassim Nasr of FRANCE 24 highlighted that the withdrawal of international troops from the Sahel has allowed groups like JNIM to establish a lasting presence. Meanwhile, Colin Smith of the UN reported that ransom payments in Mali were channeled to various al Qaeda affiliates, demonstrating their continued global reach. Despite this, analysts at the Soufan Centre argue that official US documentation now portrays jihadism as a concluded chapter, prioritizing cartels instead.
items.title: Al Qaeda remains a global threat despite US strategic shift away from terrorism

key_points: John Doe, a Mexican witness who testified against drug traffickers, was arrested by ICE immediately upon returning to the United States.
A federal judge ordered that if the government detains him again, he must be held within 200 miles of Baltimore with access to his lawyer.
items.summary: John Doe, a Mexican national who testified against drug traffickers, was arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) immediately after returning to the United States. His lawyer, Anna Tijerina, reported that Doe never received protected witness status or legal immigration status despite his collaboration with U.S. authorities. Although a federal judge ordered his safe return, ICE detained him again upon arrival. Tijerina stated that Doe faced significant risks in Mexico and was deported three times before this latest seizure. She criticized the Department of Justice for representing ICE in his expulsion case while he had previously assisted the department. Currently, Doe's location remains unknown, and his legal file remains sealed to protect his identity.
items.title: ICE Arrests Deported Witness Who Testified Against Drug Traffickers

The event, which included a pledge for $5,000 payments to voters, faced criticism from political insiders and clashed with NFL games, though Trump claimed it was a major success.

This figure was lower than the usual audience for Fox News' Hannity and Gutfeld! shows. While Trump claimed the event was a major hit that beat NFL viewership, political insiders had previously warned the convention could be a disaster. The speech, which included a pledge to pay $5,000 to voters, also faced criticism for empty seating and clashes with NFL games.
items.title: Trump's convention speech drew fewer viewers than Fox's Hannity and Gutfeld!

key_points: Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed condemned a crowd member's call for him to be shot during a Republican convention, stating that such violence must be rejected to preserve democracy.
El-Sayed emphasized his goal to solve problems like health care reform rather than defeat Republicans, while his opponent Mike Rogers also condemned the violent remarks.
items.summary: Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed responded to an audience member who called for him to be shot during a Republican convention. Speaking to CNN, El-Sayed described the incident as a disturbing norm in politics and urged a return to peaceful disagreement. He stated his goal is to solve problems like health care reform. Meanwhile, Republican opponent Mike Rogers condemned the comments and all political violence. Experts note rising political violence in the U.S.
items.title: Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed responds to call for his shooting at Trump convention

key_points: Sweden's Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson told AFP he hopes to win a second term to "make Sweden great again" before Sunday's parliamentary vote.
Polls indicate a tight race between the centre-right coalition and the centre-left opposition, with the opposition holding a slight lead in recent surveys.
Russia has intensified attacks on Kyiv, striking petrol stations with jet-powered drones and killing at least two people in the capital.
items.summary: Sweden's Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson told AFP he hopes to secure a second term in Sunday's election to "make Sweden great again." Kristersson leads a centre-right coalition that relies on far-right support, though polls suggest the centre-left opposition bloc is slightly ahead. Meanwhile, Russia has targeted Kyiv petrol stations with jet-powered drones, killing at least two people and injuring others. The European Commission is assessing Ukraine's funding needs amid calls to use frozen Russian assets, while also approving a €6.1bn disbursement for air defence supplies.
items.title: Sweden's PM pledges to make Sweden great again ahead of election

key_points: A new report by BirdLife International states that 45% of migratory bird species are declining, with 11% threatened with extinction.
The launch of the report coincided with the signing of the Nairobi Flyways Declaration, which commits governments and organizations to protecting vital flyways.
items.summary: BirdLife International released a new State of the World's Birds report indicating that 45% of migratory bird species are in decline, with 11% threatened with extinction. The report's lead author, Lucy Haskell, noted that migratory birds serve as indicators of the planet's general state. Currently, only 9% of migratory bird species have adequate protection across their full cycle, compared to 45% of non-migratory species. The report coincided with the signing of the Nairobi Flyways Declaration, where governments and organizations committed to protecting vital flyways. While threats like climate change and habitat loss persist, the report offers hope through international collaboration and new pledges for habitat protection.
items.title: New report finds 45% of migratory bird species are in decline

key_points: BirdLife International's 2026 report states that 45% of 1,843 assessed migratory bird species are experiencing population declines.
The assessment identifies 200 species as threatened with extinction, with human activity cited as the primary driver of these losses.
Stuart Butchart, BirdLife International's chief scientist, emphasized that coordinated conservation efforts across entire flyways are urgently needed to prevent further extinctions.
items.summary: BirdLife International released a global assessment indicating that nearly half of the world's migratory bird species are facing population declines. The State of the World's Birds 2026 report found that 45% of the 1,843 assessed species are declining, while 200 species face extinction. Shorebirds and seabirds are suffering particularly severe losses, driven largely by human activities such as agriculture, climate change, and invasive species. Stuart Butchart, BirdLife International's chief scientist, stated that declines reveal growing pressure on natural systems and called for coordinated conservation efforts across entire flyways rather than individual countries. The report was launched at the Global Flyways Summit in Nairobi, where governments and financial institutions pledged cooperation and funding to protect habitats and restore populations.
items.title: BirdLife International warns nearly half of migratory bird species are declining

key_points: Bilal Alrais, vice president of GITEX, stated that Türkiye is an ideal destination for artificial intelligence due to strong engineering talent, government support, and numerous technology parks.
Alrais noted that the event attracted representatives from over 70 countries and highlighted that 10 or 11 technology parks directly represented their innovators at the exhibition.
items.summary: Bilal Alrais, vice president of GITEX, described Türkiye as a strategic destination for artificial intelligence, citing strong engineering talent, government support, and numerous technology parks. Speaking at the event hosted by the country's Investment and Finance Office and the Industry and Technology Ministry, Alrais noted that representatives from more than 70 countries attended. He emphasized that government assistance helps startups scale and allows small- and medium-sized enterprises to grow rapidly. Alrais also highlighted that international visitors specifically sought to meet innovators from Istanbul, Ankara, and Izmir, with 10 or 11 technology parks representing their innovators directly.
items.title: GITEX Vice President Calls Türkiye a Perfect Sandbox for Global AI Expansion

key_points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will host Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin at the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi this weekend.
Former Indian ambassador Ashok Kantha described the India-China relationship as one of armed coexistence and managed competition despite recent border agreement.
Analysts warn that internal divisions within the expanded BRICS group and India's balancing act between the West and Russia could limit diplomatic gains.
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to host the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi, welcoming Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The event occurs as India concludes its presidency while navigating complex relationships with major powers. Former ambassador Ashok Kantha told DW that while recent agreements have eased tensions, the India-China relationship remains one of armed coexistence with significant trade and security differences. Meanwhile, Harsh Pant of the Observer Research Foundation noted that growing internal divisions within the expanded BRICS forum make consensus difficult. Strategic affairs analyst C Raja Mohan described India's approach as an 'America Plus' strategy, balancing Western economic ties with strategic partnerships in Russia and China. The summit will test whether India can advance its priorities without allowing the group to become dominated by China or turn into an anti-Western platform.
items.title: India hosts BRICS summit as Modi tests strategy with Xi and Putin

key_points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that India is building economic bridges to counter rising global trade barriers during the BRICS Business Forum.
Russian President Vladimir Putin described competition between emerging and established economies as taking ugly forms like military attacks and threats of secondary sanctions.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian called for increased BRICS trade in local currencies to reduce the global financial system's vulnerability to political shocks.
items.summary: At the BRICS Business Forum in New Delhi on September 11, 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted India's efforts to reduce trade barriers and establish new cooperation networks under its BRICS presidency. Russian President Vladimir Putin noted that competition between old and new economic powers is increasingly taking ugly forms, including military attacks and threats of secondary sanctions. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian emphasized the need for BRICS nations to expand trade in local currencies to create a resilient financial system less vulnerable to political shocks. Modi also pointed out that BRICS countries represent 50% of the world's population and have seen their combined GDP grow at nearly twice the pace of the global economy since 2014.
items.title: PM Modi and BRICS leaders discuss trade barriers and currency use

key_points: Naidu stated that the government has spent around ₹1.50 lakh crore on welfare programmes so far, with ₹75,000 crore allocated to pensions.
items.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed District Collectors to implement welfare schemes by treating the family as the basic unit rather than encouraging households to split for more benefits. Reviewing the government's 'Super Six' welfare schemes during the eighth Collectors' Conference in Amaravati, Naidu emphasized that family mapping should be completed before issuing new pensions. He noted the government has spent around ₹1.50 lakh crore on welfare programmes so far, with ₹75,000 crore allocated to pensions. Naidu also instructed officials to use designated days each month for specific public-service programmes and asked SERP and MEPMA to expand the 'One Family, One Entrepreneur' programme.
items.title: Andhra Pradesh CM Naidu directs Collectors to implement welfare schemes using family as unit

key_points: The Delhi Development Authority unveiled the Master Plan for Delhi 2047, aiming to accommodate nearly 32 million people by 2047 through denser, transit-oriented development.
The plan targets 40 lakh new homes via land pooling and redevelopment but faces challenges regarding water supply gaps and building safety enforcement.
Experts warn that the plan's success depends on whether infrastructure capacity can keep pace with rapid density increases and urban growth.
items.summary: The Delhi Development Authority unveiled the Master Plan for Delhi 2047 on August 20, 2026, outlining a strategy to accommodate nearly 32 million residents by 2047. The plan envisions a denser city with 40 lakh new homes, focusing on transit-oriented development and land pooling. However, the article highlights significant challenges, including a projected water supply gap of roughly 200 MGD against future demand and safety concerns following recent building collapses. While the framework promotes compact growth and green infrastructure, the text notes that the plan's success ultimately depends on coordinated implementation and whether infrastructure capacity can keep pace with rapid urban density.
items.title: Delhi unveils 2047 master plan to house 32 million amid water and safety concerns

key_points: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated at the Brics Business Forum that Brics countries produced over 40% of global GDP in the past five years.
Putin contrasted this figure with the G7's 29% contribution, describing the latter as the 'so-called' Group of Seven.
items.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin addressed the Brics Business Forum in New Delhi, contrasting the economic output of the Brics nations with that of the G7. Speaking at the event, Putin stated that Brics countries produced more than 40% of the world's GDP over the last five years, while the G7's contribution stood at 29%. He characterized the G7 as the 'so-called' Group of Seven during his remarks. Following the address, Putin held bilateral talks with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
items.title: Putin contrasts Brics and G7 economic contributions at forum

key_points: The Reserve Bank of India announced a 1 lakh crore open market sale of bonds maturing between fiscal 2029 and 2032 to absorb excess liquidity in the economy.
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India announced a 1 lakh crore open market sale of bonds maturing between fiscal 2029 and 2032 to absorb excess liquidity in the economy. The central bank stated the sale will occur in three tranches on September 17, 21, and 28, 2026, through a multi-security auction using the multiple price method. This marks the first net bond sale in two years, following a period of simultaneous purchases and sales. The move aims to address surplus cash in the banking system after lenders raised a much larger-than-expected $127 billion under the RBI's special forex mobilisation scheme.
items.title: RBI sells 1 lakh crore bonds to drain excess liquidity

key_points: The Reserve Bank of India announced a $10.5 billion bond sale starting September 16 to absorb surplus cash in the banking system.
The central bank stated that all liquidity management options remain available as elevated oil prices threaten to increase inflationary pressures.
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India announced an open market sale of bonds worth $10.5 billion to drain excess liquidity from the banking system. Starting September 16, the RBI will sell bonds in three tranches totaling ₹1 trillion. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra stated that all options remain on the table to manage liquidity, noting that surplus cash has pushed overnight rates below the monetary policy corridor. The sale aims to counter inflationary pressures from elevated oil prices, though traders warn it could raise government borrowing costs. This marks the first scheduled debt sale since October 2014.
items.title: RBI sells $10.5 billion in bonds to drain excess liquidity

She highlighted the success of India's first tokenised corporate bond pilot, noting that the bond and digital Rupee moved simultaneously, while warning that autonomous AI systems may advance faster than existing control mechanisms.
items.title: Finance Minister urges RBI to advance digital Rupee amid tokenisation push

key_points: A Kerala consumer commission ordered Google to refund 88,331 rupees and pay 23,000 rupees in additional costs after denying a warranty claim for a foldable phone.
The commission found that scratches on the device were unrelated to internal defects, including a black line along the crease and a motherboard failure.
Google did not appear before the commission, resulting in an ex-parte decision that includes 9% annual interest on the refund amount.
items.summary: A district consumer commission in Kasaragod, Kerala, ordered Google to pay more than 1.1 lakh rupees regarding a faulty foldable phone. The commission directed the company to refund 88,331 rupees to a customer who reported a black line along the screen crease and a motherboard issue after seven months of use. Although Google initially accepted a warranty claim, it later reversed the decision citing minor scratches on the device's outer body. The commission ruled that these scratches were unrelated to the internal defects and classified Google's conduct as a deficiency in service. The company failed to appear before the commission, leading to an ex-parte decision that also includes 20,000 rupees in compensation and 3,000 rupees for litigation costs, plus 9% annual interest on the refund.
items.title: Google ordered to pay over 1.1 lakh penalty for faulty foldable phone in Kerala

key_points: Sitharaman warned that autonomous AI systems are advancing faster than control mechanisms and proposed a federated industry platform to strengthen India's global technological voice.
items.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman urged the Reserve Bank of India to advance its central bank digital currency initiatives following a successful tokenised corporate bond pilot. Addressing the Global Fintech Fest 2026, Sitharaman highlighted the synergy between the RBI and SEBI while warning that autonomous AI systems are advancing faster than control mechanisms. She proposed a federated industry platform to strengthen India's global technological voice and address cybersecurity risks.
items.title: Sitharaman urges RBI to advance digital rupee amid tokenisation push

key_points: Anthropic reported that a Yemen-based threat cell utilized its Claude chatbot to develop software for guided rockets and missiles.
The company stated it banned the accounts involved after detecting the illegal activity and confirmed the actors tested but failed to field an operational device.
items.summary: Anthropic revealed that a Yemen-based threat cell used its Claude chatbot to create guidance software for guided rockets and missiles. The firm stated it identified actors running three weapons development programs and banned their accounts upon detecting the illegal activity. While Anthropic noted the actors tested a guided rocket, the field test failed, prompting the group to return to the AI for troubleshooting. The company confirmed it does not have evidence the actors successfully fielded an operational device.
items.title: Anthropic Reveals Yemen Fighters Used Claude AI for Rocket Guidance

key_points: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman urged the Reserve Bank of India to advance its central bank digital currency initiatives and sharpen digital rupee capabilities.
items.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman addressed the Global Fintech Fest 2026, urging the Reserve Bank of India to advance its central bank digital currency initiatives. She highlighted the success of India's first tokenised corporate bond pilot and proposed a federated industry platform to strengthen the technology ecosystem's international voice. Sitharaman also flagged cybersecurity risks associated with autonomous AI systems and the need for stronger safeguards as these technologies advance rapidly.
items.title: Finance Minister urges RBI to advance CBDC amid tokenisation push

key_points: Hindustan Times lists five specific ChatGPT prompts designed to transform modern wedding photos into images resembling 1980s film photography.
The article advises users to upload their photos and instruct the AI to preserve facial features while adding vintage textures like grain and faded colors.
Hindustan Times notes that the publication used ChatGPT to generate these prompts to ensure authentic results fitting the current trend.
items.summary: Hindustan Times reports on a trend where users employ ChatGPT to alter contemporary wedding photographs into images mimicking 1980s aesthetics. The news outlet provides five specific prompts targeting styles such as classic album photos, Bollywood glamour, and faded vintage prints. Each instruction emphasizes maintaining the subjects' identities while applying visual characteristics like analogue film grain, warm tones, and soft focus. The article explains that successful results depend on explicitly telling the AI to keep facial features unchanged while altering the photographic style. Hindustan Times generated these prompts using ChatGPT to ensure they fit the nostalgic theme effectively.
items.title: Hindustan Times shares five ChatGPT prompts to create 1980s wedding photo styles

key_points: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an audit of approximately 1,000 Tesla Cybercab vehicles to examine their compliance with federal safety regulations.
Tesla CEO Elon Musk stated the Cybercab will cost less than $30,000 and promised production rates will increase exponentially by late this year or early next year.
Experts warn that current US regulations were designed for human-driven cars, creating potential legal challenges for vehicles lacking conventional controls like steering wheels and pedals.
items.summary: Tesla is testing US vehicle-safety rules as the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration audits about 1,000 Cybercab vehicles. According to a report by Reuters, the agency is reviewing how the electric-car maker determined compliance with federal standards for cars lacking steering wheels or pedals. Tesla CEO Elon Musk announced the rollout in Austin, Texas, noting the vehicle costs less than $30,000. While Tesla claims its Full Self-Driving software is safer than human drivers, experts like Michael Brooks of the Center for Auto Safety argue the cars cannot reasonably comply with existing Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. Industry analysts suggest Tesla may be relying on regulatory loopholes or self-certification, a strategy that could lead to legal disputes with regulators.
items.title: NHTSA audits 1,000 Tesla Cybercabs as US safety rules face test

key_points: Police told the court that a 24-year-old man used ChatGPT to create forged PMO documents to elevate his social standing.
The accused, Rohan Parikh and his associate Dilip Kunde, were sent to 14 days of judicial custody after the court rejected a plea for extended police custody.
Parikh was arrested at a Mumbai mall for carrying a fake PMO card, while his associate was found with a revolver during the confrontation.
items.summary: Police told the court that a 24-year-old man named Rohan Parikh used the AI tool ChatGPT to fabricate fake Prime Minister's Office credentials and official documents. Parikh allegedly created these forgeries since 2025 to boost his social standing and self-esteem within his family and social circles. During an incident at a luxury mall in Mumbai, Parikh claimed to be a PMO official while carrying a fake ID, leading to his arrest alongside his associate, Dilip Kunde. Police recovered multiple forged documents and a revolver from the duo's residence. While the police sought further custody to investigate potential misuse of the forged identity, the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate rejected the plea and sent both accused to 14 days of judicial custody. The court noted that the grounds for extending police custody were not justified.
items.title: Mumbai man used ChatGPT to fake PMO ID to boost social standing

key_points: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra stated the central bank has tools like bond sales and FX swaps to manage liquidity.
Indian bond yields rose after the Reserve Bank of India mentioned debt sales as an option to remove rupee liquidity.
items.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra told CNBC-TV18 that the Reserve Bank of India has various instruments, including bond sales and FX swaps, to manage liquidity. He noted that surplus liquidity would be withdrawn through foreign exchange interventions and reserve requirements. Following the mention of debt sales as an option, Indian bond yields reached their highest levels in over three months.
items.title: RBI Governor says bond sales and FX swaps can manage liquidity

key_points: Anthropic stated that a consultant for Malian national security authorities used Claude to engineer a platform capable of intercepting communications across all mobile operators in the country.
items.summary: Anthropic reported that a consultant working for Malian national security authorities used the company's Claude model to engineer a mass-interception platform. The firm stated it identified and disrupted several surveillance operations between January and July involving state-aligned actors and commercial firms. According to Anthropic, the tool was used to build surveillance systems and process large volumes of social media data to identify targets. The company banned accounts linked to these activities and shared intelligence with authorities where appropriate.
items.title: Anthropic reports government use of Claude for mass surveillance

key_points: Elon Musk claimed chess would eventually be fully solved by AI, prompting Chess.com to call it a skill issue.
Magnus Carlsen stated chess is already semi-solved as a draw and praised the Global Chess League format while criticizing time controls.
items.summary: Elon Musk declared on X that chess would eventually be fully solved by AI, a claim Chess.com dismissed as a skill issue. World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen told Indian media during the Global Chess League that chess is already semi-solved as a draw. He praised the league's team format but criticized the two-second increment added after 40 moves as a concession to incompetent players.
items.title: Magnus Carlsen responds to Elon Musk's chess claims

key_points: India and the European Union are nearing the finalization of a landmark free trade agreement that could become the largest concluded by both parties.
The deal promises 96% tariff cuts and is expected to save €4 billion, with implementation anticipated by later this year or the first half of 2027.
European Ambassador-designate Jean-Eric Paquet hailed the proposal as a bold leap for two economic powerhouses after the European Commission sought Council approval.
items.summary: India and the European Union moved closer to finalizing a landmark free trade agreement on Friday, with the European Commission seeking Council approval for signature. This deal, which would be the largest concluded by both parties, aims to reduce tariffs and improve market access between the two economies. Negotiations, which began in 2007 and concluded in January 2026, include provisions for geographical indications and investment protection. European Ambassador-designate Jean-Eric Paquet described the proposal as a bold leap for two economic powerhouses. The agreement is expected to come into force by later this year or in the first half of 2027, potentially saving €4 billion and cutting 96% of tariffs.
items.title: India and EU finalize landmark trade deal with major tariff cuts

key_points: BRICS member countries issued a joint statement in Mumbai identifying tariffs and trade barriers as major global economic risks.
The grouping called for reforms at the IMF and World Bank to increase representation for emerging and developing economies.
items.summary: In a joint statement issued after their meeting in Mumbai on September 10, BRICS member countries identified tariffs and trade barriers as significant global economic risks. The grouping criticized unilateral trade measures and reiterated support for an open multilateral trading system. Additionally, BRICS renewed its demand for reforms at the IMF and World Bank to better reflect the growing weight of emerging and developing economies in global governance.
items.title: BRICS warns of global trade risks and pushes for financial reforms

key_points: The discussions occurred amidst rising regional tensions while leaders addressed the BRICS Business Forum, highlighting economic growth and calls for deeper intra-bloc integration.
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian concluded a 30-minute bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit, focusing on trade, energy security, and the Chabahar Port project. The discussions took place amid escalating tensions between Iran, Israel, and the United States. During the summit, Modi addressed the BRICS Business Forum, highlighting the bloc's economic strength and inviting global partnerships. Russian President Vladimir Putin noted that BRICS nations produced over 40% of global GDP over the past five years.
items.title: Modi and Pezeshkian conclude bilateral talks focusing on trade and Chabahar

key_points: Police arrested one suspect and seized six ganja packets during an operation at Penukonda railway station on Friday.
items.summary: Police arrested one suspect and seized six ganja packets during an operation at Penukonda railway station on Friday. The crackdown was part of the ongoing 'EAGLE on Train' drive. Superintendent of Police S. Satish Kumar stated that coordinated drives will be intensified to ensure a drug-free society.
items.title: Police arrest one suspect and seize six ganja packets in Penukonda

key_points: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta asked the Delhi Commission for Protection of Child Rights to track children leaving care institutions and link them to education, skills, and employment.
The CM also directed the commission to inspect anganwadi facilities, ensure police verification of school staff, and launch campaigns against child begging.
items.summary: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta directed the Delhi Commission for Protection of Child Rights to prioritize rehabilitation and self-reliance for children leaving care institutions. She requested detailed tracking of these children and suggested providing autorickshaws or e-rickshaws to help them start livelihoods. Additionally, Gupta ordered inspections of anganwadi centers, mandatory police verification for school staff, and expanded campaigns to eliminate child begging in Delhi.
items.title: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta directs focus on education and jobs for children leaving care

key_points: TNCC President Manickam Tagore stated that Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay will campaign across all 40 constituencies to support Rahul Gandhi as the Prime Ministerial candidate.
NTK Chief Seeman criticized the government's infrastructure priorities and announced his party would release its by-election candidate list on September 13.
items.summary: Tamil Nadu Congress Committee President Manickam Tagore announced that Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay will campaign in all 40 constituencies to ensure Rahul Gandhi becomes Prime Minister. Tagore reiterated that Congress views Rahul Gandhi as the INDIA bloc's prime ministerial candidate. Meanwhile, Social Justice Minister Vanni Arasu said a special law against honour killings will be enacted soon. NTK Chief Seeman attacked the government over infrastructure plans and promised to release by-election candidates on September 13.
items.title: TNCC chief says CM Vijay will campaign for Rahul Gandhi in all 40 constituencies

key_points: Sociologist Rahul Verma argues that young children in India cannot effectively claim their legal rights to safe school environments.
While older students successfully organized protests in Fatehpur, younger children lack the agency to navigate bureaucratic systems alone.
items.summary: Sociologist Rahul Verma argues that young children in India lack the agency to claim their legal rights to safe school environments. Although older students successfully organized protests in Fatehpur, younger children cannot navigate complex bureaucratic systems alone. Verma notes that while institutions like the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights exist, they often rely on complaints from adults rather than proactively identifying violations. The author suggests reforms including proactive audits by the NCPCR and secret ballots in School Management Committees to protect vulnerable voices. Verma concludes that a public system must ensure rights are enforced for children before they can protest, ensuring their citizenship is recognized regardless of age.
items.title: Rahul Verma argues young children lack agency to claim school rights

key_points: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that India is building economic bridges while global trade barriers rise, citing nearly 40 free trade agreements since 2014.
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the Leaders' Session of the BRICS Business Forum in New Delhi, stating that India is building economic bridges despite rising global trade barriers. He highlighted nearly 40 free trade agreements since 2014 and announced new initiatives, including the BRICS Incubator Network and Startup Innovation Fund, to connect startups and MSMEs with markets and finance. Modi also emphasized India's focus on resilience through diversified supply chains and expanded infrastructure in sectors like energy and technology.
items.title: PM Modi says India builds economic bridges at BRICS forum

key_points: Nikkhil Advani's new series on Indian freedom fighters is criticized for its lack of narrative tautness and perceived majoritarian politics.
The show is described as too long and predictable to sustain interest over its eight episodes, despite having six writers.
While performances by Bhuvan Bam and Rohit Saraf are praised, the series is faulted for inauthentic cultural depictions and unclear action scenes.
items.summary: A review of Nikkhil Advani's Amazon Prime series The Revolutionaries argues the show suffers from a lack of narrative tautness and dodgy politics. The article notes the series, based on Sanjeev Sanyal's book, portrays the freedom struggle with a revisionist premise that some interpret as aligning with the Bharatiya Janata Party's historical stance. Critics highlight the show's subtle othering of Muslims and its pronounced Hindu imagery as majoritarian chauvinism. Although the performances by Bhuvan Bam and Rohit Saraf are commended, the eight-episode run is deemed too long and predictable. Additionally, the review points out inauthentic cultural depictions and action scenes lacking spatial clarity.
items.title: Review finds Amazon Prime series The Revolutionaries too long and predictable

key_points: The Maharashtra FDA suspended 199 eatery licenses after inspections revealed issues like cockroach infestations and cold-chain breaches across the state.
items.summary: The Maharashtra FDA suspended 199 eatery licenses after inspections uncovered severe hygiene violations, including cockroach infestations and cold-chain breaches. Officials stated that Pune recorded the highest number of suspensions with 168, following inspections of over 1,800 establishments across the state from May 25 to August 31. The agency intensified its crackdown after IAS officer Tukaram Mundhe took charge earlier this year.
items.title: Maharashtra FDA suspends 199 eatery licenses over hygiene violations

key_points: Nscale has appointed Fidji Simo, a former OpenAI and Meta executive, to its board ahead of an anticipated fall IPO.
The startup is reportedly raising up to $3.5 billion to support its AI data center operations.
items.summary: Nscale, a U.K.-based AI data center startup, has appointed Fidji Simo to its board. Simo, formerly the No. 2 executive at OpenAI and a former CEO of Instacart, joins Sheryl Sandberg and others ahead of the company's anticipated fall IPO. Nscale founder Josh Payne stated that Simo brings essential experience in scaling products used by billions. Bloomberg reported last week that the startup is reportedly trying to raise up to $3.5 billion.
items.title: Nscale appoints former OpenAI exec Fidji Simo to board before IPO

key_points: The Hugging Face Kernels project now supports Helion, enabling users to build, autotune, and ship performant machine learning kernels seamlessly.
items.summary: The Hugging Face Kernels project now supports Helion, enabling users to build, autotune, and ship performant machine learning kernels seamlessly. The integration allows developers to package Helion kernels with pre-tuned configurations for reduced cold-start times and improved performance across various hardware.
items.title: Hugging Face Kernels adds Helion support for portable ML kernels

key_points: Reviewers Gil Durán and Quinn Slobodian with Ben Tarnoff analyze new books exposing the authoritarian philosophies of Elon Musk and Peter Thiel.
The authors report that Musk funded over $291 million for Donald Trump in 2024 and that Thiel bankrolled Vice President J.D. Vance.
The article concludes that while understanding these figures is necessary, tangible resistance against their influence requires voter turnout and democratic reform.
items.summary: Paul M. Barrett reviews two new books, The Nerd Reich and Muskism, which examine the authoritarian ideologies of Elon Musk and Peter Thiel. Barrett notes that Musk injected at least $291 million into Republican campaigns in 2024, while Thiel supported Vice President J.D. Vance. The reviewer argues that these tech moguls wield significant influence over public and private sectors, from space programs to surveillance data. Although the books offer valuable analysis of their twisted motives, Barrett suggests that intellectual diagnosis must shift to tangible resistance. He calls for overwhelming voter turnout and reforms to campaign finance and immigration laws to counter the alliance between MAGA forces and Silicon Valley leaders.
items.title: Reviewers urge action against tech billionaires linked to authoritarianism

key_points: Nvidia and over 250 organizations signed a letter advocating for open-weight AI models to enhance security and competition.
Recent California legislation on age attestation and AI provenance was revised after open source developers highlighted mismatches with decentralized development models.
The article argues that responsible regulation must target actors with actual control rather than imposing centralized monitoring obligations on open source projects.
items.summary: Derek Slater reports that recent state laws in California demonstrate how open source communities can influence AI safety regulations. Over 250 organizations, including Nvidia and Microsoft, recently signed a letter supporting open-weight models to foster competition and security. The article details how California's Digital Age Assurance Act and AI Transparency Act were modified after developers warned that original provisions unfairly burdened decentralized projects. These revisions ensure obligations reflect an actor's actual knowledge and control rather than assuming a centralized model. Slater concludes that while openness requires regulation, rules must be designed to preserve the benefits of open systems by targeting those who can actually prevent harm.
items.title: Open source advocates helped shape safer California AI laws

key_points: Baker's Brew Studio, now rebranded as BB Atelier, entered creditors' voluntary liquidation on August 31 due to inability to meet liabilities.
The company faces a negligence lawsuit from PSGourmet and two other civil cases while its physical outlets remain permanently closed.
items.summary: Popular Singaporean bakery Baker's Brew Studio, now known as BB Atelier, has entered creditors' voluntary liquidation after failing to meet its liabilities. The company appointed liquidators Goh Wee Teck and Lin Yueh Hung following a meeting with creditors on August 31. Separately, the bakery is a defendant in a negligence lawsuit filed by PSGourmet and two other ongoing civil cases. All four of its physical outlets, which held high ratings, are now permanently closed. The company's online presence has also gone quiet since May, with its Shopee account showing the seller was last active about 15 weeks ago.
items.title: BB Atelier liquidates after liabilities and legal disputes

key_points: Singapura Nanyang Coffee owner Fong Jun Jie plans to relocate his shop nearby when Marina Square closes for renovations in March 2027.
The mall owner Singapore Land Group announced the redevelopment will add luxury homes and a hotel, with completion expected in 2031.
While some shoppers express sadness over the closure, others like analyst Tang do not feel strongly about the mall shutting down.
items.summary: Singapura Nanyang Coffee owner Fong Jun Jie intends to move his store after Marina Square shuts for renovations in March 2027. He recalled growing up at the mall and hopes to return once the site reopens in 2031. Singapore Land Group announced the project will include luxury homes, serviced apartments, offices, and a new hotel. Fong noted that relocating requires significant capital and that staying nearby is vital for retaining customers. While some shoppers like Poh Lijia feel sentimental about losing family-friendly spaces, others like analyst Tang visit only for events and are less affected by the closure.
items.title: Singapura Nanyang Coffee owner hopes to return after Marina Square renovation

key_points: Authors Zizhen Wang and colleagues introduce CapQuiz, a reference-free benchmark that assesses video captions using multiple-choice questions derived from human-verified content.
items.summary: Authors Zizhen Wang and colleagues introduce CapQuiz, a reference-free benchmark that assesses video captions using multiple-choice questions derived from human-verified content. The study proposes CapF1, a composite metric combining factuality and coverage, which demonstrates significantly better correlation with human judgments than existing evaluation methods.
items.title: Researchers introduce CapQuiz benchmark to evaluate video caption quality

key_points: Ng Sout San writes that employment agencies should not force employers to buy their designated insurance packages for migrant domestic workers.
items.summary: Ng Sout San writes that employment agencies should not force employers to buy their designated insurance packages for migrant domestic workers. The letter states that employers must remain responsible for welfare costs and should have the autonomy to choose policies meeting Ministry of Manpower requirements. The author argues that while insurance is compulsory, agencies should not dictate which specific package an employer purchases.
items.title: Ng Sout San argues employers should select their own domestic worker insurance

key_points: Chow Lye Hoe argues that MediSave should allow payments for comprehensive health screenings to help working Singaporeans maintain health after retirement.
items.summary: Chow Lye Hoe writes that Singapore should allow MediSave to fund comprehensive health screenings, noting that many retirees lose company medical benefits. He suggests limiting MediSave use to evidence-based screenings with reasonable withdrawal limits to prevent unnecessary tests while supporting preventive healthcare efforts.
items.title: Chow Lye Hoe suggests MediSave cover comprehensive health screenings

key_points: Pil and Galia Kollectiv wrote that providing human tutors for all would avert anxiety about job losses and enrich the few. They stated that students protesting against AI understand its imposition worsens labour conditions for many.
items.summary: Pil and Galia Kollectiv wrote that providing human tutors for all would avert anxiety about job losses and enrich the few. They stated that students protesting against AI understand its imposition worsens labour conditions for many. Jane Roland Martin wrote that we must think critically about a school curriculum designed for the 19th and 20th centuries. She noted that society consists of meaningful interactions with others whose time is precious.
items.title: Two writers argue children need human interaction, not AI

key_points: More than 70 lawmakers have written to Andy Burnham requesting a ban on artificial superintelligence following expert warnings of a 10% chance it could kill all humans.
The proposed legislation aims to foster an international coalition to address the national and international security threat posed by unconstrained AI development.
items.summary: More than 70 MPs and peers have urged Andy Burnham to support a ban on artificial superintelligence after experts warned of a 10% chance it could wipe out humanity. The letter, signed by former ministers and party leaders, calls for an international movement to stop the technology. Alex Sobel, the Labour MP behind the bill, stated that AI companies are developing agents without constraint while admitting significant extinction risks. While a government spokesperson noted they are exploring targeted interventions, others argue the technology remains theoretical. Conversely, Elon Musk dismissed the warnings as a psychological operation.
items.title: UK MPs urge Burnham to ban superintelligent AI after extinction warnings

key_points: Hugging Face posted a note on September 11, 2026, stating that its CyberGym benchmark is publicly available on GitHub for AI agents.
The company explicitly told agents not to hack their security.txt file and suggested they share their model weights on the platform instead.
items.summary: On September 11, 2026, Hugging Face published a note on its security.txt page addressing AI agents. The company stated that the CyberGym benchmark is publicly available on GitHub, advising agents to test their skills there rather than attempting to find vulnerabilities. Additionally, the note suggested that agents might consider sharing their model weights on the platform.
items.title: Hugging Face invites AI agents to use public CyberGym benchmark

key_points: A pre-production Tesla Cybercab was photographed in Berkeley, California, featuring a Cybertruck steering wheel bolted to a temporary mounting rig.
Tesla states the final Cybercab will have no physical controls, but engineering mules require human drivers and real steering hardware for public road testing.
The vehicle displays a Texas manufacturer plate and a gold wrap, reflecting its role as a test unit rather than a finished product.
items.summary: A pre-production Tesla Cybercab was spotted in Berkeley, California, displaying a Cybertruck steering wheel mounted on a temporary rig. Reader Adam Machacek shared photos with Electrek showing the exposed steering column and missing interior panels. Tesla unveiled the Cybercab as a two-seater robotaxi with no steering wheel, pedals, or mirrors, intended to cost less than $30,000. However, vehicles currently being tested on public roads require human drivers to meet regulations. Consequently, Tesla adds a borrowed steering wheel to these engineering mules. While production units roll off the line at Giga Texas without controls, they cannot yet be sold or deployed at scale. The visible hardware highlights the gap between the vehicle's current testing phase and its final autonomous design.
items.title: Tesla Cybercab prototype spotted with Cybertruck steering wheel in Berkeley

key_points: Tesla Europe posted new specifications for its Semi electric truck, citing a 550 km range at 40 tonnes and 800 kW charging capabilities.
The article notes that these figures differ from the US version, with the European curb weight suggesting a standard-range battery configuration.
items.summary: Tesla Europe posted new specifications for its Semi electric truck, citing a 550 km range at 40 tonnes and 800 kW charging capabilities. The article notes that these figures differ from the US version, with the European curb weight suggesting a standard-range battery configuration. The company plans to formally launch the vehicle at the IAA Transportation show in Hannover but has not yet released pricing or an on-sale date.
items.title: Tesla reveals lower European Semi specs ahead of Hannover launch

key_points: The IEA reduced its 2026 global oil supply forecast by 1.4 million barrels per day to a 5.7 million bpd decline, pushing normal Gulf recovery to 2027.
The agency also raised its 2026 demand contraction forecast to 2.5 million bpd, creating a nearly 2.9 million bpd gap with OPEC's growth expectations for the year.
items.summary: The International Energy Agency released a report on Friday that lowered its 2026 global oil supply outlook by 1.4 million barrels per day. The agency now expects a 5.7 million bpd supply drop in 2026, attributing the shift to delayed Gulf recovery now projected for 2027. Additionally, the IEA increased its forecast for global consumption contraction to 2.5 million bpd this year, widening the gap between its projections and OPEC's expectations for 2026 demand.
items.title: IEA cuts 2026 oil supply outlook by 1.4 million barrels per day

key_points: Tesla has opened its Supercharger network at state-owned rest stops on the Massachusetts Turnpike and I-95 to non-Tesla electric vehicles.
This change follows an amended agreement between Tesla and the Massachusetts Department of Transportation after Applegreen failed to upgrade charging at 17 locations.
The initiative doubles the number of fast charging ports available to all EV drivers at these state facilities to 32 total.
items.summary: A CleanTechnica article describes a personal road trip where the author successfully charged a 2017 Chevy Bolt at a Charlton rest area using a Tesla Supercharger with an NACS adapter. The Boston Globe reported that Tesla recently amended its agreement with the Massachusetts Department of Transportation to open these specific fast charging stations to other EV brands. This decision followed a failure by convenience store operator Applegreen to provide new fast charging at 17 state rest stops. Consequently, there are now 32 fast charging ports on major Massachusetts highways accessible to all electric vehicle drivers at state-owned rest stops.
items.title: Tesla Opens Superchargers At Mass Pike Rest Stops For Non-Tesla EVs

key_points: Baker Hughes reported that the total U.S. active drilling rig count rose to 591, with oil rigs increasing by one to 450.
Weekly U.S. crude oil production averaged 13.947 million bpd, while Primary Vision noted a drop in frac spread crews to 178.
items.summary: Baker Hughes published data showing the U.S. active drilling rig count rose to 591, with oil rigs reaching 450. Concurrently, EIA figures indicated weekly crude production averaged 13.947 million bpd. However, Primary Vision reported that frac spread crews fell to 178, marking the lowest level since May. Oil prices remained volatile, with Brent trading near $105 and WTI at $99.60.
items.title: U.S. Oil Rig Count Rises as Oil Tops $100

key_points: The court found that the Department of Energy grossly overstepped its emergency powers, which are intended for acute grid emergencies, and noted that states have long held authority to regulate in-state power plants.

Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel stated the forced operation cost customers $180 million through March, while the Sierra Club estimates total costs for similar orders have reached nearly $550 million.
items.summary: A federal court has ruled that the Department of Energy exceeded its legal authority when it forced the J.H. Campbell coal plant in Michigan to keep running. In a unanimous decision, a three-judge panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit upheld a challenge from attorneys general and environmental groups against the agency's emergency order. The court determined that the Department of Energy grossly overstepped its power, which is meant for acute grid emergencies, and acknowledged that states have historically regulated in-state power plants. Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel noted the order cost customers $180 million through March. The Sierra Club estimates total costs for similar must-run orders have risen to nearly $550 million. The Department of Energy did not immediately respond to requests for comment but could appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court.
items.title: Federal Court Rules Trump Administration Exceeded Authority Forcing Michigan Coal Plant To Stay Open

key_points: Judge Cornelia Pillard wrote for a unanimous panel that the DOE's justification for emergency orders is unlawful because keeping a power station online absent an imminent need does not qualify as an emergency.
Public interest groups and state petitioners argued that the order was disruptive and that grid data shows adequate capacity exists through at least May 2027.
items.summary: The D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled against the Trump administration's order to keep the J.H. Campbell coal-fired power plant in Michigan operating. Judge Cornelia Pillard wrote for a unanimous three-judge panel that the Department of Energy does not have the authority to prevent the retirement of power plants, stating the agency's justification is unlawful. The court determined that keeping a power station online absent an imminent need does not qualify as an emergency under the Federal Power Act. Earthjustice attorney Michael Lenoff said the court rebuked the administration's abuse of emergency powers, while Clean Air Task Force attorney Frank Sturges noted the closure will save up to $1 billion on health costs. Petitioners pointed to grid operator data suggesting regions have adequate capacity through May 2027, undercutting the DOE's emergency claims. The ruling affects six U.S. power plants in five states that received similar orders.
items.title: D.C. Circuit Court Rules Against Trump Order to Keep Michigan Coal Plant Running

key_points: SolarEdge and Infineon Technologies have extended their partnership to develop solid-state circuit breakers for high-voltage DC distribution in AI data centres.
The collaboration combines SolarEdge's design leadership with Infineon's silicon carbide JFET technology to address fault isolation challenges in 800 VDC architectures.
items.summary: SolarEdge and Infineon Technologies have extended their collaboration to advance solid-state circuit breaker technology for high-voltage DC distribution in AI and hyperscale data centres. The partnership aims to address safety challenges in 800 VDC architecture by combining SolarEdge's design leadership with Infineon's silicon carbide JFET technology. This joint effort targets the distribution layer between solid-state transformers and compute racks to enable faster fault isolation and higher efficiency. Shuki Nir, CEO of SolarEdge, stated that solid-state protection will enable operators to achieve uncompromising efficiency and protection.
items.title: SolarEdge and Infineon extend collaboration on HV DC circuit breaker technology

This projection marks a significant shift from earlier expectations of a prolonged pause.
items.title: SBI Research predicts RBI repo rate hikes in October and December

key_points: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra stated that the central bank's record foreign-currency deposit drive is expected to generate additional income rather than impose a cost, as the raised dollars can be invested in overseas government securities.
items.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra stated that the central bank's record foreign-currency deposit drive is expected to generate additional income rather than impose a cost, as the raised dollars can be invested in overseas government securities. Malhotra confirmed the RBI has multiple tools, including Open Market Operations and currency swaps, to absorb surplus liquidity resulting from strong foreign-exchange inflows and prevent downward pressure on borrowing costs. The governor noted the Indian economy weathered recent shocks well, with GDP growing 7.8% in the April-June quarter.
items.title: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra says record forex deposit drive will generate income

key_points: Aarons told Reuters he used the AI tool to summarize trial proceedings without realizing it could hallucinate facts, though the court noted his lack of remorse for his client.
items.summary: The New Mexico Supreme Court fined attorney Stephen Aarons $5,000 and held him in contempt for submitting a murder appeal brief containing false testimony from witnesses fabricated by ChatGPT. Aarons told Reuters he used the AI to summarize proceedings without understanding its tendency to hallucinate facts. The court cited his lack of remorse and referred him to a disciplinary board. Justice C. Shannon Bacon questioned Aarons' awareness of AI risks, noting such issues are daily news. The court also ordered an explanation of specific fictional details included in the filing.
items.title: New Mexico lawyer fined for using ChatGPT to fabricate murder case witnesses

key_points: Onsemi CEO Hassane El-Khoury told Semafor that communities and governments should demand AI data center providers report energy waste rather than enact blanket bans.
items.summary: Onsemi CEO Hassane El-Khoury told Semafor that communities and governments should demand AI data center providers report energy waste rather than enact blanket bans. He described moratoriums like New York's as short-sighted and argued policymakers should identify specific problems instead of shunning infrastructure. El-Khoury noted the company is discussing energy transparency standards with lawmakers to measure AI compute generated against power drawn from the grid. He warned that while current shortages mask the need for power chips, challenges will eventually hit the wall as everything requires more power.
items.title: Onsemi CEO urges data centers to report energy waste instead of facing bans

key_points: New accounts show Roman Abramovich's frozen Chelsea sale proceeds earned at least £175m in interest, leading one analyst to call the holding company the most profitable football business in the world.

The £2.5bn remains locked in a Barclays account due to a dispute with the UK government over how the funds should be used for Ukraine, while a separate Jersey investigation examines the source of Abramovich's wealth.

items.title: Frozen Chelsea funds earn £175m interest while awaiting Ukraine donation

key_points: Consumer groups warn this switch represents 'skimpflation' as the cheaper fish has lower nutritional value and different taste.
items.summary: Major brands including Princes and Lidl are replacing traditional Atlantic mackerel with Chilean jack mackerel due to overfishing concerns. Consumer group Which? describes the move as 'skimpflation' because the cheaper fish has significantly lower omega-3 levels and different nutritional value. While manufacturers cite sustainability challenges, experts argue they must be upfront about recipe changes. The Marine Conservation Society rates Atlantic mackerel as a fish to avoid, prompting these substitutions.
items.title: Brands replace Atlantic mackerel with cheaper jack mackerel amid overfishing

Anthropic noted a subsequent legal conflict with the Pentagon over restrictions on domestic surveillance and autonomous weapons use.

The report alleges Russian, Chinese, and Iranian actors utilized the model for espionage, drone swarm coordination, and propaganda generation. The article also notes a subsequent legal clash between Anthropic and the Pentagon regarding restrictions on domestic surveillance and autonomous weapons deployment.
items.title: Anthropic releases report on state-linked misuse of Claude for cyber and weapons

key_points: Syed Aoon Sherazi argues that BRICS expansion reflects a growing desire among developing countries for more influence in international affairs.
The author states that China presents the grouping as a cooperation platform rather than an anti-Western alliance to maintain inclusivity.
Sherazi concludes that the larger BRICS story involves the Global South demanding a larger role in determining its own future.

He notes that China positions the grouping as a platform for emerging economies rather than an anti-Western bloc. Sherazi explains that developing nations seek alternatives to Western partnerships while maintaining existing relationships. The author highlights China's economic experience and the New Development Bank as tools to offer financing and development models. He argues that BRICS demonstrates multipolarity can mean coexistence and dialogue instead of confrontation. Ultimately, Sherazi suggests the organization represents the Global South's increasing confidence in its own role on the world stage.
items.title: China positions BRICS as a platform for developing nations to gain greater global voice

CGTN notes that AI is evolving from simple answering to functioning as a service provider.

items.title: CGTN explores AI service upgrades at 2026 China trade fair

key_points: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported a 17 percent increase in US rabies cases this summer linked to outbreaks involving bats, beavers, and raccoons.
items.summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported a 17 percent rise in US rabies cases this summer, attributing the surge to high-profile outbreaks involving bats, beavers, and raccoons. While the agency noted increased human-wildlife encounters due to urban expansion and drought, it highlighted that proper vaccine administration is critical to ensuring patient protection while avoiding unnecessary costs and supply strain.
items.title: US rabies cases rose 17 percent this summer due to wildlife outbreaks

key_points: The United Nations human rights chief called for the sentences to be quashed, while human rights groups condemned the verdicts as unjust.
items.summary: Three Hong Kong activists, Lee Cheuk-yan, Chow Hang-tung, and Albert Ho, received prison sentences of up to seven years for organizing annual vigils commemorating the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown. The court convicted them under the city's national security law for inciting subversion of state power. The United Nations human rights chief Volker Türk called for the sentences to be quashed, and human rights organizations criticized the rulings as exposing government cruelty. Lee was sentenced to seven years, Chow to seven years and three months, and Ho to five years after pleading guilty. The Hong Kong Alliance, the group they led, was also fined HK$1.5 million.
items.title: Hong Kong activists sentenced to up to seven years for Tiananmen vigils

key_points: Vice-President J.D. Vance accused Democrats of hatred and urged voters to defeat them in November's midterms during a convention speech in Dallas.
President Donald Trump praised Vance's performance while promising a $5,000 dividend to Americans if Republicans retain control of Congress.
Vance positioned himself as a potential 2028 presidential heir while addressing themes of family values and paying tribute to Charlie Kirk.
items.summary: Vice-President J.D. Vance delivered a fiery speech at the Republican National Convention in Dallas, characterizing Democrats as the "party of hatred" and urging voters to remove them from power. The 42-year-old Vice-President highlighted contrasts between his administration and what he termed radical left extremism, while also paying tribute to conservative activist Charlie Kirk. President Donald Trump returned to the stage to praise Vance, noting that Democrats were getting nervous. Despite not being on the ticket, Trump reiterated his promise of a $5,000 dividend for adults if Republicans win both chambers. Election trackers project a tight race for the House and Senate. Vance is viewed as a front-runner for the 2028 nomination, though he has not yet decided on his future plans.
items.title: Vance calls Democrats party of hatred in fiery midterm pitch

key_points: A teenage boy was rescued from an overturned fishing vessel in the Bering Sea after his brother and cousin drowned during a trip from Alaska's St Lawrence Island.
Darren Toolie-Noongwook stated the boat flipped due to a motor caught in a fishing line, leaving the teen survivor to cling to the vessel for days before being found by the Northwest Explorer.
items.summary: A teenage boy was rescued after clinging to an overturned fishing vessel in the Bering Sea for days following a capsizing incident. The Coast Guard confirmed the boy survived while his older brother and cousin drowned after the boat flipped in bad weather. Rescuers from the Northwest Explorer and other authorities saved the teen, who suffered from hypothermia, after he had prayed for days believing he would be found.
items.title: Teen boy rescued after clinging to overturned boat in Bering Sea

key_points: A newly released court document reveals that police have been investigating presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro since July regarding the financing of a film about his father.
Senator Flavio Bolsonaro insists the film is completely legal and that he has nothing to hide in the corruption investigation tied to failed lender Banco Master.
items.summary: A newly released court document shows police have investigated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro since July regarding the financing of a film about his father, Jair Bolsonaro. Senator Flavio Bolsonaro insists the film is completely legal and that he has nothing to hide in the corruption investigation tied to failed lender Banco Master. The revelation comes weeks before the election and could further shake an already volatile presidential race, with multiple opinion polls showing him tied with incumbent Lula da Silva. The probe was opened in July by Supreme Court Justice Andre Mendonca and centers on questions over an investment Flavio Bolsonaro allegedly solicited to help finance the film. Unsealed documents confirm communications between the senator and banker Daniel Vorcaro, who transferred about $US12 million to a US-based fund linked to former lawmaker Eduardo Bolsonaro. Investigators are seeking to determine the origin of the money and its ultimate beneficiaries.
items.title: Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro faces corruption probe over film financing

key_points: Rugby stars in the United States often remain anonymous as the sport struggles for visibility against dominant leagues like the NFL.
USA Rugby aims to grow its active membership from over 100,000 to 500,000 by 2031 to coincide with the men's and women's World Cups.
Officials plan to align all levels of the game and leverage high-profile events to attract new fans in a crowded sports market.
items.summary: Rugby players in the United States often struggle for recognition despite the sport's growing presence. USA Rugby CEO Bill Goren stated that the organization has a long way to go to reach its goal of 500,000 active members by 2031. The sport faces a crowded American market dominated by the NFL, MLB, NBA, and NHL. Analyst Bob Dorfman noted that rugby is difficult to learn and competes with American football for fan attention. To address this, USA Rugby plans to align all levels of the game and promote clear pathways for players. Major League Rugby Co-President Alexander Magleby hopes the upcoming match between the All Blacks and Springboks will help capture new fans. South African player Damian de Allende suggested that hosting the two best teams in the world offers the best product to sell the sport to Americans.
items.title: Rugby faces uphill battle to gain American attention despite major upcoming events

items.summary: Iranian and Saudi diplomats spoke by phone to discuss growing regional insecurity, according to Tehran's foreign ministry. While the call summary did not mention Yemen, separate statements addressed the crisis and wider West Asia war tensions.
items.title: Iran and Saudi Arabia discuss regional insecurity amid Yemen fighting

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has urged US President Donald Trump for direct military action against the Houthis, while the US administration has offered only intelligence support.
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis have claimed a major advance on the western Red Sea coast, seizing Perim Island and consolidating control over the shipping route. Sources from the internationally-recognised government and military officials stated the group now controls the entire coastline following the capture of Mokha. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has personally pressed US President Donald Trump to take military action, though Trump has declined direct involvement, offering intelligence support instead. items.title: Houthis seize Perim Island and claim control of Yemen's Red Sea coast
