items.title: Kremlin says Russia open to trilateral talks with US and Ukraine

key_points: The French government has joined Slovakia in seeking the delisting of Russian-Uzbek businessman Alisher Usmanov from the EU sanctions list, a move that has caused frustration among other member states.

EU ambassadors are scheduled to meet on Monday to discuss the renewal of sanctions before the 15 September deadline, with Slovakia opposing the extension and pushing for the delisting of Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman. Four EU diplomats told Euronews that the French move raised questions about motivation, suggesting economic reasons rather than security concerns.
items.title: France joins Slovakia in requesting delisting of Russian oligarch Usmanov

items.summary: The Nigerian National Assembly announced a ban on all official visits to South Africa, including online engagements, citing persistent attacks on Nigerian citizens. The decision follows deadly demonstrations in South Africa against foreigners, which the Assembly stated it could not ignore. Analysts note that high unemployment and crime in South Africa are increasingly blamed on immigrants despite government failures.
items.title: Nigeria bans all official visits to South Africa over anti-immigrant violence

key_points: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering tied to financing a film about his father, according to court documents unsealed on Friday.

The probe, opened by Supreme Court Justice Andre Mendonca, examines whether the senator committed money laundering and illicit foreign exchange after seeking investment from arrested banker Daniel Vorcaro.
The investigation intensifies a crisis within Brazil's Supreme Court as Chief Justice Edson Fachin seeks to resolve a public clash between justices Mendonca and Alexandre de Moraes.
items.summary: Brazilian presidential hopeful Flavio Bolsonaro faces a corruption probe just weeks before the national election, according to court documents unsealed on Friday. The investigation, opened by Supreme Court Justice Andre Mendonca, centers on alleged money laundering and corruption tied to financing a film about his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro. Details emerged after Chief Justice Edson Fachin ordered the Banco Master case records public, revealing federal police requests to examine the senator's dealings with arrested banker Daniel Vorcaro. This development exacerbates a severe internal crisis at the Supreme Court involving a clash between justices Mendonca and Alexandre de Moraes. Meanwhile, President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva publicly supported full disclosure of the investigation, stating that allegations involving the judiciary should be made public regardless of consequences.
items.title: Flavio Bolsonaro investigated for corruption amid tight Brazil election

key_points: Russian electoral authorities have disqualified at least 36 candidates from the September 18-20 State Duma election using flimsy justifications.
Experts note that reasons for disqualification range from posting images of banned social media logos to displaying artwork by Banksy or Motörhead founder Lemmy Kilmister.
Analysts attribute these moves to a security bloc seeking to suppress anti-war sentiment and control the political landscape during the ongoing conflict in Ukraine.
items.summary: Russian authorities are disqualifying parliamentary candidates using dubious claims as the September 18-20 State Duma election approaches. An investigation by independent media Verstka reports at least 36 candidates have been barred, including those who posted images of banned social media platforms or artwork by Banksy and Lemmy Kilmister. Experts describe these motives as absurd and intended to demonstrate that resistance is futile. The Kremlin is reportedly using these tactics to suppress anti-war sentiment and maintain control over the political landscape amidst the ongoing conflict in Ukraine.
items.title: Russian authorities disqualify candidates using dubious claims amid war

key_points: Mozambique formally protected the 9,341-hectare Mount Mabu Community Conservation Area, granting stewardship to local communities in the Lugela district.
Julian Bayliss, an ecologist who led surveys over 20 years, stated the forest is vital due to its high levels of endemism and hosts more than 200 butterfly species.
items.summary: Mozambique formally protected Mount Mabu, a biodiversity hotspot in the Lugela district, by establishing the 9,341-hectare Mount Mabu Community Conservation Area. The Ministry of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries published the decree on Aug. 24, granting stewardship to local communities who have preserved the forest for generations. Julian Bayliss, an ecologist who led surveys over 20 years, noted the area's high endemism and recorded more than 200 butterfly taxa, with the real number potentially reaching 250. The decree dedicates the land to protection and sustainable use by locals, though specific restrictions await a finalized community management plan.
items.title: Mozambique protects Mount Mabu butterfly forest for local communities

key_points: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra stated the Monetary Policy Committee will review growth and inflation dynamics at its October meeting amid rising crude oil prices.
items.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the Monetary Policy Committee will reassess growth and inflation dynamics at its October meeting due to rising crude oil prices from the West Asia crisis. Malhotra also told CNBC-TV18 that nearly 50% of the $127.22 billion in FCNR(B) deposits mobilised under the forex swap facility are for a five-year tenor, reflecting strong investor confidence in India's macroeconomic fundamentals.
items.title: RBI Governor says MPC will reassess growth and inflation at next meeting

items.title: BRICS negotiators seek consensus on Iran conflict paragraph for Delhi Declaration

key_points: Farmers in Karimnagar district staged a road blockade on Friday to protest alleged unscheduled power cuts affecting their standing maize and other crops.

Similar demonstrations occurred in Jagtial and Khammam districts on the same day.
items.title: Farmers in Karimnagar block roads demanding uninterrupted power for crops

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian called for greater use of national currencies in trade among Brics members during the summit.

items.title: Trump warns Brics over dollar while India balances US and Russia ties

key_points: Congress leader P. Chidambaram questioned tangible benefits from recent BRICS summits, prompting a debate with Shashi Tharoor.

items.summary: Congress leader P. Chidambaram questioned the tangible benefits India has gained from recent BRICS summits, stating he saw no significant outcomes. BJP leaders subsequently launched broadsides against Chidambaram and the Congress party, questioning their diplomatic record since Independence. items.title: Tharoor defends BRICS value as Congress questions benefits and BJP counters

key_points: The Reserve Bank of India issued draft amendment directions requiring banks to implement a Standard Operating Procedure for placing temporary debit holds on accounts linked to money-mule activity and cyber-enabled financial frauds.
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India issued draft amendment directions requiring banks to implement a Standard Operating Procedure for placing temporary debit holds on accounts linked to money-mule activity and cyber-enabled financial frauds. The new rules, effective from April 1, 2027, mandate that banks notify account holders within 24 hours, allow a 20-day window for explanations, and limit the maximum hold duration to 60 days. These measures follow a Supreme Court order directing the central bank to establish such procedures for combating financial fraud.
items.title: RBI issues draft SOP for temporary debit holds on money-mule, cyber fraud accounts

key_points: Microsoft plans to invest USD 17.5 billion in India from 2026 to 2029 for cloud and AI infrastructure, while the government aims to add 20,000 GPUs to the IndiaAI Mission.
items.summary: Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal met Microsoft India President Puneet Chandok in New Delhi to discuss expanding data centre capacity and advancing the India AI Mission. The Office of Piyush Goyal stated that India is emerging as a preferred destination for global tech investment. Microsoft announced plans to invest USD 17.5 billion in India from 2026 to 2029 for cloud and AI infrastructure. Meanwhile, the government aims to add another 20,000 GPUs to the IndiaAI Mission to expand national AI computing capacity.
items.title: Piyush Goyal meets Microsoft India chief to expand data centres and advance AI mission

items.title: Hindustan Times lists ten ChatGPT prompts for 1980s photo edits

key_points: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa met Adani Group Chairman Gautam Adani during the 18th BRICS Summit to deepen trade and investment links between the two nations.

The South African government stated the engagement aims to expand intra-BRICS commerce, promote industrialization, and mobilize infrastructure investment aligned with the African Continental Free Trade Area.
items.summary: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa met Adani Group Chairman Gautam Adani on Friday during the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi. The South African government posted that the meeting aims to deepen commercial and investment ties between the two countries. President Ramaphosa also addressed the India-South Africa Business Leadership Roundtable and participated in a closed BRICS leaders session focused on global governance reform. The delegation included ministers Ronald Lamola and Khumbudzo Ntshavheni, who supported the President during his visit.
items.title: South African President Meets Gautam Adani to Strengthen Trade Ties

key_points: An Irish man asked Grok how long it would take to gain Indian citizenship after arriving in Kolkata.
Elon Musk responded to the interaction on X by stating, 'India is realistic' regarding the lengthy process.
items.summary: An Irish man traveling to Kolkata inquired about the timeline for obtaining Indian citizenship via the xAI chatbot Grok. The AI explained that naturalisation requires at least 12 years of lawful residence and the mandatory renunciation of his Irish nationality due to India's policy against dual citizenship. Elon Musk commented on the exchange on X, praising the country's approach. He stated, 'India is realistic.' The article notes that the user also asked about financial assistance and property ownership, receiving answers that highlighted the lack of social welfare for non-citizens and the dependency of home buying on residency status. Live Mint published the story based on social media content without independent verification.
items.title: Elon Musk praises India after Irish man learns citizenship takes 14 years

key_points: The accused were remanded to judicial custody after police recovered a laptop, hard drive, and purported PMO documents from his residence in Khar.
items.summary: Mumbai police told a court that 24-year-old Rohan Parikh allegedly used ChatGPT to create fake Prime Minister's Office documents since 2025 to impress others. Parikh and his bodyguard were arrested for attempting to enter Jio World Plaza while posing as PMO officials. Police recovered a laptop, hard drive, and purported PMO documents from Parikh's residence in Khar. The accused were remanded to judicial custody while authorities investigate the firearm used by the bodyguard and examine electronic devices. The matter was adjourned to September 17, 2026, for a police reply.
items.title: Mumbai Police Say Man Used ChatGPT To Forge PMO Documents

key_points: Anthropic reported blocking attempts by bad actors to use its AI models for cyberattacks, surveillance, and biological weapon research.
The company added stronger safeguards in its latest models to restrict dual-use biological research that could enhance pathogens like chikungunya.
Anthropic published a misuse report following a researcher's resignation over concerns regarding AI safety and the potential for self-improving superintelligence.
items.summary: Anthropic announced Thursday that it blocked malicious attempts to use its artificial intelligence models for cyberattacks, surveillance, and biological weapon research. The company stated it has implemented stronger safeguards in its latest models to restrict biological research that could be used to create weapons. In a report released in August 2026, Anthropic detailed instances where actors sought assistance for gain-of-function research on the chikungunya virus. The startup noted that while older models were less capable of assisting in dangerous research, newer models require stricter controls. This disclosure follows a resignation by researcher Jacob Coxon, who warned that the industry is racing toward self-improving superintelligence without sufficient oversight. Anthropic urged governments and competitors to identify similar abuse patterns as models become increasingly powerful.
items.title: Anthropic Blocks AI Misuse for Biological Weapons and Cyberattacks

key_points: The India-EU Free Trade Agreement provides a tariff-rate quota of 100,000 units annually for EU-origin internal combustion and hybrid vehicles priced above Euro 15,000.
The pact also includes concessional tariffs on wines, pork, apples, kiwifruit, pears, and peaches, with duties declining over five to eleven years.
items.summary: The India-EU Free Trade Agreement establishes specific tariff-rate quotas for European vehicles and agricultural products. Under the deal, the EU receives a quota of 100,000 completely built-up internal combustion and non-plug-in hybrid cars annually for the first five years, provided they are priced above Euro 15,000. GTRI Founder Ajay Srivastava highlighted that this allocation is almost six times the 17,191 cars India imported from the EU in 2025. Beyond automobiles, the agreement offers concessions on wines, pork, apples, kiwifruit, pears, and peaches, with duties gradually reducing over several years. These commitments apply only to imports meeting specific origin, price, and quantity conditions, while excess imports face normal tariffs. The agreement is expected to be signed by year-end and may come into force next year.
items.title: India grants EU tariff quotas for 1 lakh cars and other goods

key_points: The European Commission forwarded proposals to the European Council on Friday to conclude the India-EU free trade agreement by the end of the year.
European Commission President Maroš Šefčovič stated that the pact will eliminate or reduce tariffs on 96% of EU goods exports to India, saving around €4 billion annually.
The agreement is expected to enter into force early in 2027 after clearance by the European Parliament and Indian ratification procedures.
items.summary: The European Commission has advanced the India-EU free trade agreement by forwarding signing proposals to the European Council, aiming for a formal conclusion by year-end. Negotiations concluded in January after a decade-long hiatus, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi expected to visit Brussels for the signing. The European Commission described the deal as the largest trade agreement ever between the two entities, noting it will eliminate tariffs on 96% of EU goods exports to India. Following signature, the pact requires ratification by the European Parliament and Indian authorities before entering into force early in 2027. Trade volumes currently exceed €180 billion annually, with the agreement promising enhanced market access and reduced barriers.
items.title: EU Commission forwards proposals to finalise India-EU free trade deal by year-end

key_points: Anthropic released a 154-page report identifying how AI models were used for cyberattacks, espionage, and biological weapons research between December 2025 and August 2026.
The company stated that attackers increasingly use AI to automate multiple steps of malicious operations, including targeting 50 organizations in a Chinese-linked espionage campaign.
Anthropic accused Alibaba of attempting to copy Claude's capabilities through a distillation process involving over 151 million exchanges between May and July 2026.
items.summary: Anthropic published a 154-page report detailing how artificial intelligence is being misused for malicious activities. The company said it identified and disrupted attempts to use its Claude models for cyberattacks, espionage, and biological weapons research between December 2025 and August 2026. Anthropic noted that attackers are increasingly using AI to automate multiple steps of operations, such as finding targets and stealing data, which allows for sophisticated attacks with fewer people. The report highlighted a Chinese-speaking group that targeted about 50 organizations and an automated fake news operation in Bangladesh. Additionally, Anthropic accused Alibaba of conducting the largest attempt to copy its AI capabilities, recording more than 151 million exchanges attributed to the company's activity. The findings suggest that the challenge for AI safety is preventing models from being combined with other tools to carry out real-world operations.
items.title: Anthropic report details AI misuse in espionage, biological research, and model copying

key_points: At the BRICS Business Forum in New Delhi, foreign delegates gathered around Prime Minister Narendra Modi to request a group photograph.
During the interaction, PM Modi remarked that the women in the group were lucky to be with him, prompting laughter before he thanked them.
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi emerged as a popular choice for photographs at the BRICS Business Forum in New Delhi on Friday. A video shared by the Government of India on X showed delegates approaching him and asking, 'Can we have a picture?' PM Modi agreed, and the moment included a playful exchange where he remarked on the presence of many ladies in the group. The interaction offered a lighter glimpse of engagements at the summit, where Modi also addressed the forum and held bilateral meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.
items.title: BRICS delegates request photo with PM Modi at New Delhi forum

key_points: The National Geodetic Survey is replacing outdated reference systems NAD 83 and NAVD 88 with new frameworks aligned to modern Earth measurements.
The new horizontal system uses four frames tied to tectonic plates, while the vertical system relies on a gravity-based model called GEOID2022.
While most Americans will not see changes to their addresses, the update will significantly impact construction, surveying, and GPS precision.
items.summary: The National Geodetic Survey announced plans to update the United States' geodetic reference systems to align with modern satellite technology. The agency stated that the current North American Datum of 1983 is misaligned by about 2.2 meters and the vertical datum is biased by roughly half a meter. The new horizontal system will utilize four frames linked to major tectonic plates, while the vertical system will adopt GEOID2022 based on airborne gravity measurements. Although the physical land will not move, the numerical coordinates for locations will change to reflect these more accurate measurements. The agency noted that while home addresses will remain the same, professionals in construction and surveying will see significant improvements in centimeter-level accuracy.
items.title: US survey agency updates coordinate systems to improve accuracy

key_points: Rising Ganga waters have inundated parts of Ratua and Manikchak in Malda, forcing residents to use makeshift tin boats for survival after fifteen days of severe waterlogging.
A special administrative team led by the District Magistrate has been deployed by the Chief Minister to monitor the worsening ground situation in the district.
items.summary: The flood situation in Malda has worsened after rising Ganga waters inundated parts of Ratua and Manikchak. Local residents have endured severe waterlogging for nearly fifteen days, risking their lives on makeshift tin boats to transport rations and salvage belongings. With Civil Defence boats proving insufficient, displaced villagers seek shelter along roadsides. A special administrative team comprising the District Magistrate, Superintendent of Police, and senior bureaucrats has been deployed by the Chief Minister to monitor the situation.
items.title: Floods in Malda submerge Ratua and Manikchak as residents use tin boats

key_points: The central bank sold the 6.20% 2029 bond at a yield of 6.4566%, which was up 25 basis points over the previous four weeks.
items.summary: Traders reported that the Reserve Bank of India partially cancelled a government security auction on September 11, 2026, to prevent further bond yield increases. The central bank accepted bids worth ₹45.06 billion, representing just over 40% of the planned ₹110 billion borrowing. Consequently, the 6.20% 2029 bond was sold at a yield of 6.4566%, marking a 25 basis point rise in the last four weeks.
items.title: RBI partially cancels debt auction to curb bond yield spike

key_points: The regulator sought public comments on the proposal by October 2, 2026.
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) proposed extending the IT and cyber security framework applicable to Market Infrastructure Institutions to their subsidiaries. SEBI stated this move would ensure the regulatory framework remains aligned with evolving market structures as MIIs diversify. The regulator noted that subsidiaries sharing infrastructure or handling similar data must comply, though exemptions are possible with compensatory controls. SEBI invited public comments on the consultation paper by October 2, 2026.
items.title: SEBI proposes extending IT and cyber security rules to MII subsidiaries

key_points: PhD candidate Zil Audi-Poquillon identifies three political factors that enabled Kenya's 2023 health reform to pass where a similar 2004 attempt failed.
The author attributes the success to concentrated presidential power, the co-optation of previous opponents, and a populist framing of the reform as a fight for ordinary Kenyans.
The study notes that while the health system's problems remained unchanged, the political tactics used to bypass institutions and rush the law through remain controversial.
items.summary: PhD candidate Zil Audi-Poquillon argues that Kenya's 2023 universal health reform succeeded where a similar 2004 attempt failed due to specific political strategies rather than just timing. The author identifies three key factors: concentrating power in the presidency to bypass institutions, co-opting opponents who blocked the earlier reform, and framing the policy as a moral cause for ordinary citizens. Audi-Poquillon's research, based on interviews with 48 policy actors, suggests these tactics allowed the government to rush the Social Health Insurance Act through in six weeks. However, the author warns that while these methods helped pass the law, they reduced necessary scrutiny and public debate, leaving the reform vulnerable to future political challenges.
items.title: PhD candidate explains why Kenya's 2023 health reform succeeded after 2004 failure
